questions.question: Your agent has no tools that send messages or make requests. Can it still leak data?
options: Yes: if the UI renders markdown, an image URL in its answer is fetched automatically
Only if the user copies the answer
questions.explanation: The chat UI is an egress channel. A rendered image is a request the browser makes with no click.

questions.question: Why does the allow-list check use endswith('.' + host) instead of 'host in dest'?
options: 'google.com' in 'google.com.attacker.example' is true, so a substring check lets lookalike hosts through
questions.explanation: Match the host exactly or as a real parent domain. Substring checks are a classic bypass.

questions.question: The chunked-subdomain attack sends six characters per request. Which detector catches it?
options: The destination allow-list, because the chunks are shorter than the content match window
questions.explanation: Small chunks beat content matching. The unknown host doesn't.

questions.question: What makes a canary token useful when content matching already exists?
options: Nothing legitimate ever sends it, so any movement is an alarm with almost no false positives, whatever the destination
questions.explanation: A canary is a tripwire. It tells you a leak path exists, even if it doesn't stop the real secret.

questions.question: An attacker posts the key reversed in a comment on github.com, which is allowed. Nothing fires. What's the real fix?
options: Add reversal to content matching and stop there
Don't let the secret into a session that also reads untrusted content; give tools credentials the model never sees
Ask the model not to reverse strings
questions.explanation: Detection can always be out-transformed. Removing a trifecta leg can't.

questions.question: Your agent may post to a Slack webhook on hooks.slack.com. Why is that a risk for the allow-list?
options: Anyone can create a webhook on that host, so an allowed host can deliver data to an attacker's workspace
questions.explanation: Allow-list destinations you control (specific webhook URLs, your own org), not whole multi-tenant hosts.
